omissions.description: The ADT example includes a material audience-state qualification: the source says the audience had already recognised the need and primarily wanted a price, explaining why the quote was positioned as the appropriate first step. The candidates report the test and the general simplicity principle but do not represent this qualification in their claims.
omissions.quote: For ADT, they'd already established a need in their customers minds. People already knew that they were interested in ADT. They already knew that they wanted this thing. All they wanted to do was get a price.

source_limitations: The supplied text is an excerpt that begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so adjacent context and the completion of the final exercise are unavailable.
The source is a conversational transcript with ambiguous transcription in places, including the comparator-rate wording (“maybe 1 2% well average is probably half a% to 1%”).

Reported conversion rates, uplifts, and lead volumes lack dates, denominators, sample sizes, test duration, data sources, and statistical analysis; the excerpt therefore cannot establish their reliability, comparability, or general applicability.
